relevance_note: The paper describes four children with A20 haploinsufficiency and individual-level detail, stating that "Whole-exome sequencing identified heterozygous TNFAIP3 (NM_006290.4) mutations or deletion in all patients".
method_note: I read the paper, the schema and the rules, and wrote this JSON by hand; no script transcribed any table. Patients 1-4 are printed as the four data columns of Tables 1, 2 and 3 (headers "|  | Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Patient 3 | Patient 4 |"), and the same labels are used throughout the text, so no positional reading of stacked cells was needed; no cell in these tables uses " / " to stack values. Table 2's legend defines its symbols: '" − "means "Normal"; "/" means "patient didn’t conduct the test or scan"', and Table 1's legend defines '" − "means "Negative";" + " means "Positive"'; I used those definitions for the excluded rows. I created no rows for the parents of Patients 1, 3 and 4: the paper reports them only as wild-type on parental testing, which is not an individual-level fact about them as relatives (they are not described as having a variant or an HA20 diagnosis). Contradiction 1: Table 3 prints Patient 4's nucleotide change as "c.1247_1251del" while the text, abstract and Fig. 4 caption print "c.1243_1247del"; I kept the table string as variant_original_string and quoted the text string in a second span. Contradiction 2: the text says "Autoantibody panels, rheumatoid factor, skin prick test and pathogen screening were negative" for all patients, while Table 2 prints "RF-IgA elevated" for Patients 1, 2 and 4 and "Negative" for Patient 3; I emitted both phenotypic_features rows and left the checklist item "autoantibodies (ANA/other)" not reported for Patients 1, 2 and 4. Contradiction 3: Table 3 prints "de novo" for Patient 2, but the paper prints a parental-testing statement only for Patients 1, 3 and 4, so I left Patient 2's inheritance not reported (rule 8 requires the statement). Other notes: per D-27 I recorded "Anemia" as observed for all four patients from the named-group statement in the Discussion that "all four patients demonstrated anemia (likely secondary to chronic gastrointestinal bleeding) with Patient 2 exhibiting severe anemia requiring hematological intervention", with evidence_basis "inferred from group statement" and the severity detail only for Patient 2. I recorded no vasculitis row: the general discussion sentence about "missense variants" and "cutaneous vasculitis" is not stated for these four patients and is not a named group containing them; for the same reason I did not infer "recurrent infections" for Patients 2 and 3 from that general sentence, and only Patient 1 and Patient 4 have a named statement. I recorded no functional_evidence_statement; the paper reports no functional assay for any of these variants. Growth failure, pericarditis or other serositis, interstitial lung disease, autoimmune thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes and autoimmune hepatitis are never mentioned for these patients, so those checklist items are "not reported".

The resulting severe impairment of A20 function manifested as significant gastrointestinal symptoms and recurrent infections, with suboptimal therapeutic response.
